title: Offer and the power of acceptance
shortTitle: Offer and the power of acceptance
summary: An offer communicates willingness to enter a bargain in a way that reasonably gives the recipient the power to conclude it by accepting.
notes:
The question is whether the speaker has invited assent that will finish the bargain, or has invited further negotiation. Specific language, the surrounding exchange, the audience, and remaining decisions all matter. An advertisement is often an invitation for customers to make offers, but Lefkowitz treats a definite first-come advertisement differently. The identity of the offeror matters because the offer determines what response can accept it.

Restatement § 24 and the accompanying commentary focus on whether further assent by the proposer is contemplated. A price quotation, advertisement, order, or document titled “proposal” must be read in context. Lefkowitz’s limited first-come offer differs from an invitation for customers to place orders. International Filter shows why preparing a form does not necessarily make its drafter the offeror.
